question: The pair of equations 3x - 5y = 7 and -6x + 10y = 7 have:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare the ratios of the coefficients: a₁/a₂, b₁/b₂, and c₁/c₂.

a₁/a₂ = 3 ÷ (−6) = −1/2

b₁/b₂ = (−5) ÷ 10 = −1/2

c₁/c₂ = 7 ÷ 7 = 1

Since a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the lines are parallel.

**∴ The correct answer is no solution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation 1: 3x − 5y = 7

Equation 2: −6x + 10y = 7

**Formula Used:**

For a pair of linear equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂:

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the system has no solution.

**Calculations:**

⇒ a₁ = 3, b₁ = −5, c₁ = 7

⇒ a₂ = −6, b₂ = 10, c₂ = 7

⇒ a₁/a₂ = 3 / (−6) = −1/2

⇒ b₁/b₂ = (−5) / 10 = −1/2

⇒ c₁/c₂ = 7 / 7 = 1

⇒ Here, a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂

⇒ The lines are parallel and do not intersect.

**∴ The correct answer is no solution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unique Solution (Intersecting Lines)

If a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, the system of linear equations is consistent and has exactly one solution.

Infinitely Many Solutions (Coincident Lines)

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂, the system is consistent (dependent) and has infinite solutions.

No Solution (Parallel Lines)

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.
